1.0 Purpose
The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure is to define the standardized steps for cleaning, disinfecting,
inspecting, and documenting a designated workstation before it is released for routine use.
This example demonstrates the expected structure and writing style for a controlled SOP. It uses imperative language
such as must for requirements and may for permitted options.
2.0 Scope
2.1 This procedure applies to designated office, laboratory-support, or operational workstations where routine surface
cleaning and disinfection is required.
2.2 The procedure covers preparation, visual inspection, cleaning, disinfectant application, verification, and record
completion.
2.3 Out of Scope: specialized equipment decontamination, chemical spill response, electrical maintenance, and any
process requiring a separate validated cleaning procedure.
3.0 Key Terms
Term
Definition
Approved disinfectant
A cleaning/disinfection product authorized by the applicable site process or local procedure.
Contact time
The period for which the disinfectant surface must remain visibly wet, as specified by the
approved product instruction.
Workstation
The defined work area including the work surface, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and adjacent
high-touch items.
Visual inspection
A check confirming that the surface is free of visible dirt, residue, waste, and unnecessary items.
4.0 Roles and Responsibilities
Role
Responsibilities
Process Owner
Owns the procedure, ensures local applicability, and coordinates periodic review.
Operator / User
Performs the cleaning steps, follows safety instructions, and completes the record.
Quality / Reviewer
Performs periodic checks of records and confirms that deviations are handled according to applicable
processes.
Facilities / Support
Maintains cleaning supplies and removes damaged or unsuitable equipment when identified.
